 Player Stats

 Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and DeAndre Jordan will start Saturday’s game against the Nuggets. 
 With Yves Missi suffering a bone bruise in his knee during Friday’s loss to the Jazz, the Pelicans had a hole to fill at center. Instead of Derik Queen, Jordan will fill the void. While an interesting choice, Jordan offers better defense than Queen. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Derik Queen puts up 12 points (4-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and a three in 29 minutes against Jazz. 
 Queen got more minutes in this game because of the injury to Yves Missi. He’s worth a pickup in redraft leagues with the understanding that there is a chance Mosley leans into Matkovic if Queen doesn’t play defense. If Queen starts putting up good numbers, it will be a great opportunity to try and sell if Missi is going to come back at some point this season. 
 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Derik Queen had 2 points, (1-of-3 FGs), 7 rebounds, 5 assists, and two blocks against the Wizards. 
 With Yves Missi starting every game in the pre-season, Queen will likely be coming off the bench to start the season. While he can put up very fun fantasy numbers when he gets the minutes, the defense has been a problem. In addition, transitioning to Jamahl Mosley who is a defensive minded coach, it’s likely that he won’t utilize Queen’s offensive ability to a high degree. 
 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Derik Queen amassed five points (2-of-3 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and one block in Thursday’s exhibition against the Heat. 
 As of Thursday evening, Queen had a Yahoo! ADP of 85. That’s pretty high, especially for a player who isn’t guaranteed a starting role once the regular season begins. Yves Missi (11 points, nine rebounds), a superior defender, started at center in New Orleans’ two preseason games. First-year head coach Jamahl Mosley could very well go with Queen once the games count, but he’ll have to do more as a defender to make that happen. Given the uncertainty, using a top-100 pick on Queen is risky. 
 DeAndre Jordan 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #6 
 Pelicans re-signed DeAndre Jordan to a two-year contract. 
 Jordan, who turns 38 in July, will return to New Orleans for his 19th NBA season. Contract terms weren’t disclosed initially, but it was later revealed that it is a two-year deal for the veteran’s minimum. Jordan appeared in only 12 games for the Pelicans last season. He offers bench depth and a veteran presence at this point in his career. 
 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel, VJ Edgecombe, Dylan Harper and Cedric Coward were named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team on Wednesday. 
 Flagg, Knueppel, and Edgecombe all received 100 first-place votes, with Harper’s 93 votes not far behind. Cedric Coward’s 29 first-place votes were the least of the first-teamers. Meanwhile, Derik Queen, Maxime Raynaud, Jeremiah Fears, Ace Bailey, and Colin Murray-Boyles were named to the All-Rookie Second team. 
 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Derik Queen tallied 30 points (11-of-28 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 22 rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Queen finished his first NBA season with the first 30/20 game of his pro career. With the Pelicans only playing seven players on Sunday, the rookie center logged 41 minutes in the season finale. Queen recorded a complete stat line against the Timberwolves, making the low field-goal percentage more palatable. Queen certainly had his moments this season, but improvement on the defensive end of the floor is what will unlock his full potential in the years to come. 
 Zion Williamson 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Zion Williamson (knee), Yves Missi (finger) and Karlo Matković (back) will miss Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 The continued absences of Williamson and Missi are most impactful, as Derik Queen and Kevon Looney have served as the starting power forward and center. That should remain the case on Sunday, with Queen more likely to play starters’ minutes. As for Matković, his continued absence does not significantly affect the Pelicans’ rotation. 
 Saddiq Bey 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #41 
 Saddiq Bey (rest) and Herbert Jones (rest) are out for Friday’s matchup with the Celtics. 
 Bey and Jones will join the rest of New Orleans’ regular starters and Karlo Matković (back) on the bench, as the Pels will have to turn to Jeremiah Fears, Derik Queen, Jordan Hawkins and Micah Peavy to shoulder the load. 
 Yves Missi 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #21 
 Yves Missi (hand) is out for Friday’s game against the Celtics. 
 Missi remains out with a sprained right hand, freeing up additional minutes for Derik Queen. Queen started Tuesday’s win over the Jazz and nearly recorded a triple-double. The rookie should play plenty in New Orleans’ final two games of the season, regardless of Missi’s availability. 
 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Derik Queen notched 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz. 
 Recording his 12th double-double of the season, Queen finished Tuesday’s victory three assists shy of his third triple-double. And much to the delight of the Pelicans, the rookie center enjoyed one of his most impactful games as a defender. More active on that end of the floor, Queen recorded three steals and two blocked shots. Having veteran Kevon Looney (7/12/6/2/1 with one three-pointer) on the floor likely helped, but that should not be used to take away from Queen’s performance.

 Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
 Allen hasn’t started in place of Kon Knueppel (hamstring), but he has been able to fill the shooting void. That included a clutch four-point play in this game, which gave the Hornets a lead that they didn’t relinquish. Allen is rostered in just 33 percent of Yahoo! leagues, but with how many threes Charlotte shoots as a team, Allen should be rostered until Knueppel returns.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dennis Schröder

 Guard 
 #17 
 Player Stats

 Dennis Schröder lit up the Heat with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers on Saturday.
 After struggling in Friday’s blowout loss to the Hawks, Schröder was able to bounce back with his best performance of the season. Two of his three starts in place of Coby White (calf) have been productive, with the one poor performance coming in a 47-point loss that was bad for the entire team. Schröder is worth streaming until White returns to the lineup. He’s currently rostered in just 26 percent of Yahoo! leagues.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Brandon Miller

 Forward

 Player Stats

 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.
 Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.
 Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights. Any extra value he can add in other categories will just be a cherry on top.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2

 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Pelle Larsson 
 MIA

 Pelle Larsson provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (5-of-9 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Hornets on Saturday.
 After a rough start to the year offensively, Larsson was able to get things going in this one. He totaled nine points on 1-of-9 shooting across his first two outings, so this performance was a huge step in the right direction. Larsson was a late-round flier for fantasy managers hoping he would take a step forward for the Heat this season. He’s trending in the right direction, but he’ll need to produce to this level more consistently to be worth keeping rostered.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Bam Adebayo finished with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Saturday against the Hornets.
 It has been a rough start to the year for Bam, but after totaling 19 points in Miami’s first two games, he was able to surpass that mark in this one. It wasn’t enough for them to get in the win column, but it was good to see him have a productive outing. He’ll try to build on this performance in their next game, which comes against the Mavericks on Monday.
